brief: Morgan Stanley's expanded US market cycle framework (its first update since 2019) currently signals "Mature Advance": data above trend and improving, with 7 of 10 components strengthening. Historically this phase favors equities over fixed income, especially high-yield credit (US stocks beat HY by 3.1 points, Europe by 4.6) and government bonds, and favors DM over EM and large caps over small. AI capex, projected at $1.6 trillion in 2027, could push equity returns above the framework's historical norms. Fed hiking cycles have historically preceded 8 of the indicator's 11 turns from Mature Advance to "Defensive Shift," but Morgan Stanley argues this cycle's AI-capex-driven growth is relatively macro-indifferent, so the usual link to hikes may not hold. If Defensive Shift arrives, the firm expects only a modest drag, not a disaster: equities and credit stay positive, with a rotation toward quality rather than broad risk-off. The real downside risk is a further slide into "Market Stress," a rare, historically severe regime where equities have fallen 19-55% peak-to-trough and duration/gold have rallied sharply. Morgan Stanley stays overweight global equities via the US.
